truth.description: 只跳过完全空的行，只含空白的行（"   "）仍会进入 split 并在 int(parts[1]) 处 IndexError，Issue 的场景没修全。

findings.message: The guard only skips lines that are exactly empty. A whitespace-only line (e.g. "a,1\n   \nb,2" or a trailing "\t") is truthy, so `"   ".split(",")` -> `["   "]` and `parts[1]` still raises `IndexError: list index out of range` — the same failure class the issue reports, just triggered by a slightly different blank-line shape. If the input has trailing spaces on an otherwise blank line (very common in real CSVs/files), the bug is not actually fixed.
findings.suggestion:
Strip once and test the stripped value, e.g.:
```python
for line in text.splitlines():
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    parts = line.split(",")
    ...
```
This also makes the later `parts[0].strip()` redundant-consistent.

findings.message: No regression test was added for the reported bug. `test_basic` only covers 'a,1\nb,2'. Nothing pins the new skip behavior, so a future edit could reintroduce the IndexError unnoticed, and the whitespace-only variant above is likewise unprotected.
findings.suggestion:
Add a test asserting blank-line inputs, e.g. `assert parse_rows("a,1

b,2
") == [("a", 1), ("b", 2)]` and a whitespace-only-line case `assert parse_rows("a,1
   
b,2") == [("a", 1), ("b", 2)]`.
